Its debut was marked by a storefront crowded with congratulatory flowe

roles: second shop / sister brand of Fukakusa Seimen Shokudo
chef_bio.background: Menya Ikku opened on April 10, 2018, about a one-minute walk from JR Nishioji Station as the second shop and sister brand of Fukakusa Seimen Shokudo, a well-regarded ramen maker based in Fushimi Ward. Its debut was marked by a storefront crowded with congratulatory flowers. The space is deliberately stylish and modern, closer to a cafe-bar than a traditional ramen counter, with an upper floor above the ground-floor dining room.
chef_bio.philosophy: Coax maximum depth from quality regional chicken through long, careful simmering, presented in a clean, design-forward setting rather than a rough-and-ready ramen joint.
chef_bio.specialty: A rich chicken paitan (tori-paitan) ramen. The broth concentrates the umami of three heritage chicken breeds, including Nagoya Cochin, simmered with aromatics like garlic and ginger for roughly eight hours. The shop offers chicken shoyu, chicken shio, and paitan variations, plus a spicy mazesoba (karauma mazesoba). Bowls are finished with pork and chicken chashu, green onion, and premium hosaki menma (tender bamboo shoot tips) over house noodles from Menya Teigyaku.

anecdotes.text: The broth is built from three heritage chicken breeds including Nagoya Cochin, simmered roughly eight hours with aromatic vegetables to concentrate the chicken umami.
Opened in 2018 about a one-minute walk from JR Nishioji Station, with the debut storefront surrounded by many congratulatory flowers and styled like a cafe-bar rather than a typical ramen shop.
Noodles are sourced from Menya Teigyaku (麺屋棣鄂), and bowls use premium hosaki menma (bamboo shoot tips) rather than standard menma.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi（QkH9w）が2018年4月開店・JR西大路駅徒歩1分・開店祝いの花・カフェバー風の内装・2階の存在・穂先メンマを確認。osumituki（106373）が名古屋コーチンなど地鶏3種を約8時間炊いた鶏白湯、ニンニク・生姜、麺屋棣鄂の麺を確認。親ブランドは伏見の深草製麺食堂。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The menu centers on shoyu (soy-sauce-based) and shio chicken ramen; standard ramen shoyu tare is wheat-based, and no gluten-free tare is indicated.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All broths are animal-based (long-simmered chicken paitan/clear chicken soup) and bowls are topped with pork and chicken chashu, so vegan diners cannot be accommodated.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, busy local counter ramen shop with no English noted and cash-only payment, so a little Japanese or a translation app and a willingness to order at the counter will make the visit smooth.

kyr_menya_kiyo_ichijoji.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. This is a shoyu ramen specialist built on wheat: house-made wheat noodles fresh each morning, a wheat-based soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, and a dashi/shellfish broth. Gyoza and other sides also contain wheat. No gluten-free menu, no dedicated equipment, and noodles cook in shared water. A celiac diner cannot be safely accommodated here.
kyr_menya_kiyo_ichijoji.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The core bowls are built on a pork (chashu) and shellfish dashi (oyster/clam/shrimp) broth, and the signature draw is the customer-thickness-cut pork chashu simmered over two hours. No vegan or vegetarian ramen is offered; even side dishes center on pork. A strict vegan would have nothing suitable on the menu.
kyr_menya_kiyo_ichijoji.notes: 麺屋 聖 ～kiyo～ opened on October 1, 2018 as the second shop of Kyoto's Menya Yukou group, planting its flag on Ichijoji's famously competitive ramen street. Its stated mission is to carry Kyoto's dashi (出汁) culture from this neighborhood out to Japan and the wider world.

chef_bio.origin: Kyoto (Ichijoji, Sakyo Ward); second branch of the Menya Yukou group founded in Kawaramachi-Oike, Kyoto.
chef_bio.background: 麺屋 聖 ～kiyo～ opened on October 1, 2018 as the second shop of Kyoto's Menya Yukou group, planting its flag on Ichijoji's famously competitive ramen street. Its stated mission is to carry Kyoto's dashi (出汁) culture from this neighborhood out to Japan and the wider world.
chef_bio.philosophy: The parent group runs on the idea that staff are not employees but companions (仲間); the original shop was even named after its manager rather than its owner to honor that spirit. At kiyo the kitchen wants guests simply to taste the depth of the dashi and shoyu, with the chashu fat melting into the broth.
chef_bio.specialty: A mellow Kyoto-style shoyu chuka-soba served as three signature bowls (each around 800 yen). The flagship 'Gifto' is built on a shellfish-and-flying-fish dashi — asari clam and tobiuo — married to a soy-sauce kaeshi and balanced so neither the dashi nor the soy overpowers. The house-made noodles are pressed fresh every morning at the group's own noodle factory for a chewy, firm (モチモチとしたコシのある) bite, and the slow-simmered pork chashu is cut to the thickness each guest prefers right at the counter. The three bowls carry playful names: Gifto, Simple (シンプル), and Shirushi (しるし).

anecdotes.text: The pork chashu is tenderized by a unique method and simmered for over two hours, then sliced to the customer's chosen thickness at the counter.
kiyo was the Menya Yukou group's second shop, opened October 1, 2018 on Ichijoji's fiercely competitive ramen street with the aim of spreading Kyoto's dashi culture to Japan and the world.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式（yukou-kiyo.com）が麺屋優光グループ2号店、仲間思想、店長名を店名にした由来、自社製麺所で毎朝製麺、2時間以上煮込みカウンターで厚さを選べるチャーシューを確認。kyoto.tips と検索結果が2018年10月1日開店、一乗寺、1番人気『ギフト』がアサリと飛び魚出汁の醤油ラーメン、メニューはギフト／シンプル／しるし各800円と確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: House-made wheat noodles are boiled to order in shared ramen water; no gluten-free preparation exists, so cross-contamination with wheat is unavoidable.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The broth's defining element is a special soy-sauce (shoyu) tare made with traditional Kyoto soy sauce; Japanese soy sauce is normally brewed with wheat, so the broth contains wheat-derived gluten.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broth is built on shellfish dashi (oyster, clam, shrimp) and the shop's centerpiece is pork chashu; no vegan or vegetarian bowl is offered, so there is no animal-free option to protect from cross-contact.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, busy counter ramen shop on Ichijoji's competitive ramen street; ordering is typically in Japanese and the flow is quick, so a little Japanese or a translation app helps, though pointing at the menu works fine.

kyr_namae_no_nai_ramen_ya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free safe for celiacs. This is a classic ramen/tsukemen shop: wheat noodles, a soy-based tare (Japanese soy sauce almost always contains wheat), and meat/fish broths. Even the signature bowls that mention burdock or "less wheat-heavy" texture are not gluten-free, and no GF menu, GF noodles, or dedicated prep is advertised. Anyone with celiac disease or a wheat allergy should treat this shop as unsafe.
kyr_namae_no_nai_ramen_ya.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The menu is built around animal-based broths (seafood/niboshi, chicken, and pork) and the proteins offered are offal (motsu), chashu pork, and wagyu beef. There is no vegan or vegetarian ramen option, and the tare/broth foundations are animal-derived. Vegans cannot be accommodated here.

It is run as a sister project of well-known Kyoto ramen shops Tak

roles: sister shop of Takakura Nijo and Sugari
chef_bio.background: Tucked into a B1F space along the Takasegawa canal at Kiyamachi-Sanjo, this is the famous "ramen shop with no name" — there is no signboard and no storefront marking, just an unmarked staircase leading underground. It is run as a sister project of well-known Kyoto ramen shops Takakura Nijo and Sugari, and the same obsessive attention to detail carries through here.
chef_bio.philosophy: Understated elegance over conventional ramen-shop styling: the room reads more like a hidden cafe, chopsticks, napkins and condiments are tucked away in drawers beneath the counter for a minimalist presentation, and bowls are served on premium tableware (Royal Copenhagen, Staub). Diners are encouraged to adjust the flavor themselves using condiments kept at the counter.
chef_bio.specialty: A modular bowl ordered from a ticket machine: choose your noodle style (ramen, tsukemen, or curry tsukemen), your broth (delicate, layered, or rich), and your protein (offal, chashu, or wagyu beef). The layered seafood-leaning broth is a signature — described as so clean and balanced you can drink it straight — finished with charred and roasted vegetables, including roasted tomato, as accents.

anecdotes.text: The shop deliberately has no name and no sign — you reach it by an unmarked underground staircase beside the Takasegawa canal, which is part of its hidden-gem appeal.

Condiments, chopsticks and napkins are stored neatly in drawers rather than displayed, and food is served on Royal Copenhagen and Staub tableware — the space feels like a hidden cafe rather than a ramen shop.
It is run as a sister/subsidiary shop of the popular Kyoto ramen establishments Takakura Nijo (麺屋高倉二条) and Sugari (和醸良麺すがり).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi（5WVKH）が屋号も看板もないB1F店・木屋町三条・高瀬川沿い・券売機での麺/スープ/具の選択・ロイヤルコペンハーゲン/ストウブの器・ローストトマトなどを確認。ぐるなび取材と系列解説が麺屋高倉二条・和醸良麺すがりと同系列であることを確認。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature broths are described as soy-based; Japanese soy sauce used in ramen tare almost always contains wheat, so the tare should be assumed to contain gluten.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broths are animal-based (seafood/niboshi, chicken, pork) and proteins are offal, chashu pork, and wagyu beef; there is no vegan option and animal products are pervasive in the kitchen.

cultural_comfort.note: A signboard-less, locals-in-the-know spot with a touch-panel ticket machine and a modular Japanese-language menu; some Japanese ability or studying the menu beforehand makes ordering much smoother.

kyr_kanton_goryori_takeka.gf_detail: No gluten-free accommodation is indicated. This is a Cantonese restaurant whose signature dishes (spring rolls in wheat wrappers, sweet-and-sour pork, fried rice seasoned with soy sauce) rely heavily on wheat: wheat-flour wrappers, soy-sauce-based seasonings, and likely wheat starch/flour for frying. No sources mention gluten handling, a dedicated fryer, or wheat-free options. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_kanton_goryori_takeka.vegan_detail: Not a vegan venue. The kitchen does cook some vegetable-forward dishes — notably a water-spinach (空心菜) stir-fry and other seasonal-vegetable plates praised for light, gentle Kyoto-style seasoning — but these are prepared in a meat-and-seafood kitchen and the seasonings are soy/oyster-style sauces of unknown composition. A vegan could potentially eat a vegetable plate but only after asking carefully; no dedicated vegan menu exists.
kyr_kanton_goryori_takeka.hours_raw: 17:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:20); banquets/course parties until 21:30. Closed Tuesdays. Lunch banquets available by reservation for parties of 10+.
kyr_kanton_goryori_takeka.notes: Takeka opened in 1966 at the foot of Gion Shinbashi, beside the Shirakawa stream, and has spent close to six decades cooking for the geiko and maiko, teahouse patrons, and locals of the district. Its first owner trained at Fuyo-en (芙蓉園), one of the foundational houses of Kyoto's

roles: owner-proprietor (female proprietor, descendant of the geisha Takeka)
chef_bio.background: Takeka opened in 1966 at the foot of Gion Shinbashi, beside the Shirakawa stream, and has spent close to six decades cooking for the geiko and maiko, teahouse patrons, and locals of the district. Its first owner trained at Fuyo-en (芙蓉園), one of the foundational houses of Kyoto's distinctive Cantonese tradition, before going independent. The shop's name comes from Takeka, the proprietor's great-grandmother, a celebrated Gion geisha of the Taisho and early Showa eras; her vintage hairpins and combs are still displayed in the restaurant.
chef_bio.philosophy: A gentle, light, 'Kyoto-fied' Cantonese cooking that deliberately omits pungent aromatics — garlic, onion, ginger — so that the food would never interfere with a geiko's or maiko's work. The result is a refined, understated cuisine built around seasonal vegetables and clean flavors.
chef_bio.specialty: Spring rolls (春巻き) are the house signature, said to be ordered by roughly 80% of customers: a homemade crepe-like wrapper packed with finely shredded bamboo shoots, pork and crab, then cut into eight small pieces specifically so geiko could eat them without smudging makeup or staining a kimono. Also renowned are the sweet-and-sour pork (酢豚), the glossy sweet-vinegar meatballs, the roast pork (焼豚), and a fried rice (やきめし) that the kitchen has quietly refined over the years.

anecdotes.text: The spring rolls are deliberately cut into eight small bites so that geiko and maiko could eat them cleanly without ruining their makeup or kimono.
Dishes such as the sweet-and-sour pork are made without garlic, onion or ginger so the lingering aromas would not interfere with the geiko's evening work.
The restaurant is named after Takeka, the present proprietor's great-grandmother, a famous Gion geisha; her old hairpins and combs are still on display in the shop.
Cultural figures including Kitaoji Rosanjin (北大路魯山人) and the painter Hashimoto Kansetsu (橋本関雪) are said to have visited the establishment.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotokurasu（19091）が1966年創業・祇園白川沿い・初代の芙蓉園修業・曾祖母である祇園芸妓『竹香』に由来する店名と現存する簪や櫛・芸妓のためにニンニク/玉ねぎ/生姜を使わない調理・八つに切る春巻き・酢豚・焼豚・北大路魯山人や橋本関雪の来店を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No sources address gluten or wheat cross-contamination. As a Cantonese kitchen serving wheat-wrapper spring rolls and soy-sauce-seasoned dishes alongside fried items, cross-contact with wheat should be assumed pervasive.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Signature dishes such as the roast pork are seasoned with soy sauce, and the soy sauce is not specified as wheat-free; standard Japanese/Chinese soy sauce contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Vegetable dishes (e.g., the water-spinach stir-fry) are cooked in a kitchen handling pork, crab and other seafood; no vegan separation is indicated.

positives.text: The kitchen's gentle, aromatics-free Kyoto-Cantonese style means many dishes are lightly seasoned and free of garlic, onion and ginger, which may help diners avoiding those specific ingredients.

cultural_comfort.note: A long-established Gion neighborhood Chinese restaurant beloved by geiko and maiko; service is in Japanese and the experience suits a diner comfortable navigating a traditional local establishment, ideally with some Japanese or a guide.

kyr_ra_men_hi_wa_mata_noboru.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The bowls center on house-made wheat noodles (now a whole-wheat flat thick noodle for tsukemen) and a fermented soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, served over chicken-and-pork-bone broth. No gluten-free menu, dedicated equipment, or wheat-free noodle/tare options were found; a celiac-safe meal is not realistic here.
kyr_ra_men_hi_wa_mata_noboru.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The house specialty is a chicken-and-pork-bone (tori-tonkotsu) double broth simmered with ~130kg of bones per batch; a beef-bone broth variant is also offered. Toppings include chashu pork belly and house-made pastrami. No vegetable- or plant-based broth or vegan menu was found.
kyr_ra_men_hi_wa_mata_noboru.hours_raw: 11:00–21:00; closed Wednesdays. A Jiro-style option is offered after 18:00.
kyr_ra_men_hi_wa_mata_noboru.notes: [Mom & Pop] An independent neighborhood ramen shop on the busy approach street near Fushimi Inari, run by representative Shunji Otsubo under his company Hinobo. The shop relocated to its current spot by the Keihan Fushimi Inari station front, growing into a local favorite that now also draws

chef_bio.origin: Kyoto (Fushimi-ku, Fukakusa), near Fushimi Inari Taisha
chef_bio.background: An independent neighborhood ramen shop on the busy approach street near Fushimi Inari, run by representative Shunji Otsubo under his company Hinobo (株式会社ヒノボ). The shop relocated to its current spot by the Fushimi Inari station front, growing into a local favorite that now also draws the steady stream of shrine visitors.
chef_bio.philosophy: A stated belief in valuing the natural flavor of the ingredients and keeping food safe enough for children to eat: the kitchen avoids leaning on chemical umami additives, relying instead on careful preparation and heat control to get a broth that is rich but clean-finishing rather than heavy, seasoned with naturally fermented soy sauce.
chef_bio.specialty: Tori-tonkotsu ramen and a rich tsukemen: a chicken-and-pork-bone double broth simmered 8+ hours from roughly 130kg of bones per batch, paired with house-made noodles. The tsukemen broth is kept hot in a stone bowl and topped with seared pork-belly chashu and house-made pastrami, menma and green onion.

anecdotes.text: The broth is built from about 130kg of chicken and pork bones simmered for over eight hours per batch, aiming for a result that is concentrated yet elegant with a clean aftertaste.

The tsukemen dipping broth is served in a heated stone bowl to hold its temperature, with whole-wheat flat thick noodles and house-made pastrami plus seared pork-belly chashu among the toppings; it has become a draw for local ramen fans despite the touristy location.
The shop relocated from near Kintetsu Fushimi station to its current spot by Fushimi Inari, where it sits on the busy Sandan-kaido approach drawing both tourists and locals.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイトが代表 大坪俊次・運営 株式会社ヒノボ・1回の仕込みで鶏ガラと豚骨130kgを8時間強火で炊く・うま味調味料を極力排除・子どもも安心・天然醸造醤油を確認。kyotopi（p7WqE）が近鉄伏見駅前から伏見稲荷への移転、参道（三段街道）立地、石鍋のつけ麺、自家製パストラミ、全粒粉入り平打ち太麺を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Bowls are built on house-made wheat noodles and a fermented soy-sauce tare, so the dish is wheat-based throughout; no gluten-free preparation or separate handling is mentioned.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Seasoning uses naturally fermented soy sauce (and a tamari-style soy sauce for the beef-bone variant), which is wheat-containing unless specified otherwise; no wheat-free tare is offered.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The 'naturally fermented soy sauce' half is unsourceable and should be deleted. The tamari half inverts the usual trap: this is one of the rare cases where a named たまり really is 小麦不使用, so writing that it 'is wheat-containing unless specified otherwise' is a false negative a

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broths are animal-based (chicken-and-pork bone, plus a beef-bone option) and toppings include pork chashu and pastrami; there is no separate vegetable broth line, so vegan separation is not possible.

positives.text: The kitchen states it avoids chemical seasoning additives and prioritizes ingredient safety so that even children can eat the food, relying on careful preparation rather than synthetic umami enhancers.

cultural_comfort.note: A busy counter ramen shop on the main approach near Fushimi Inari that draws both tourists and locals; basic Japanese greetings help but you can manage with minimal Japanese, and there is an English site/menu.

kyr_kyoto_chuka_hamamura_fuc.gf_detail: No gluten-free options. The signature noodle dishes — 中華そば and the famous からしそば — use wheat noodles, and the からしそば is finished with a wheat-thickened ankake sauce and mustard. Chinese-style cooking here relies on soy sauce and wheat-based seasonings throughout. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_kyoto_chuka_hamamura_fuc.vegan_detail: Not a vegan-friendly restaurant. The Kyoto-Chinese cooking is built on chicken-bone and kombu dashi plus pork, and broths/sauces are animal-based. No dedicated vegan menu was found. Core items are not plant-based.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hamamura Hozo (founder, 濱村保三); third-generation Hamamura Yoshiyuki (濱村吉行)
chef_bio.background: Hamamura was founded in 1924 (Taisho 13) and is widely credited as the birthplace of Kyoto Chinese (kyo-chuka). What began as a humble noodle-and-Chinese shop grew into one of the city's defining culinary lineages, now run by the founder's grandson, the third-generation Hamamura Yoshiyuki. The Fuchomae branch sits across from the Kyoto Prefectural Office and moved to this Marutamachi spot from Kawaramachi around 2014.
chef_bio.philosophy: Kyoto Chinese holds back the garlic and heavy oil of mainland Chinese cooking, leaning instead on chicken-bone and kombu dashi for a clean, restrained flavor. The style is said to have grown out of Kyoto's geisha districts, where strong-smelling foods were discouraged.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature dish is karashi-soba: noodles bound in a glossy ankake sauce sharpened with vinegar-loosened Japanese mustard, described as spicy yet paradoxically light and refined. Their straightforward chuka-soba is the other anchor of the menu.

anecdotes.text: Hamamura is regarded as a legend of Kyoto Chinese, tracing back to the original Shina-ryori Hamamura credited with founding the kyo-chuka genre in 1924.
The karashi-soba is celebrated as spicy from the mustard yet still light and refined, a one-plate symbol of Kyoto Chinese.
The Fuchomae location relocated from Kawaramachi around 2014 and is known as an easy place to drop into, even for a solo diner.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: shinise.tv が1924年（大正13年）創業・京都中華発祥の店・創業者 濱村保三・三代目 濱村吉行・ニンニクや油を控え鶏がらと昆布の出汁を使う京都中華・芸妓文化に由来する薄味・看板のからしそばを確認。kyotopi（7lvle）が府庁前店は約5年前（2014年頃）に河原町から移転したことを確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat noodles, wheat-thickened ankake sauce, and soy/wheat seasonings are central to the menu; no gluten-free handling or dedicated equipment information was found.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard Chinese soy-sauce-based seasonings are used throughout; assume wheat-containing shoyu unless the shop confirms otherwise.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broths and sauces are built on chicken-bone and kombu dashi with pork dishes prominent; shared woks and stocks make vegan separation unlikely.

cultural_comfort.note: A welcoming, long-running neighborhood Chinese restaurant where solo and first-time visitors fit in easily; a little menu guidance helps since service is in Japanese.

kyr_ramen_mata_koko_de.gf_detail: Not safe for gluten-free or celiac diners. The signature draw is house-made extra-thick wheat noodles (極太手揉み麺), and the tare is a soy-sauce (wheat-based) seasoning over a pork-bone broth. No gluten-free noodles, separate prep, or allergen accommodation is offered or mentioned.
kyr_ramen_mata_koko_de.vegan_detail: This is a Jiro-style ramen shop built on a pork-bone (tonkotsu) broth with back fat and pork toppings; the bowls are fundamentally pork-based with mounded vegetables on top. No vegan or vegetarian option is offered or mentioned anywhere.
kyr_ramen_mata_koko_de.hours_raw: Hours 11:00–14:00 / 17:00–22:00; Fri 17:00–22:00; Sun 11:00–16:00. Closed Mon. (Note: Tabelog listing shows 11:00–15:00 / 18:00–22:00, closed Mon & Thu — local/shop sources give the times used here.)
kyr_ramen_mata_koko_de.notes: [Mom & Pop] The shop is the realization of a 13-year dream for owner-chef Takuya Kozasa, who trained for 13 years at the influential Kyoto Jiro-style house 'ラーメン荘 地球規模で考えろ／そら' (Ramen Sho 'Chikyu-kibo de Kangaero' / Sora) before striking out on his own. It opened on October 6, 2025.

chef_bio.origin: Kyoto (Nishi-Shichijo, Shimogyo Ward) — opened in the former premises of the ramen shop Akamon (赤もん)
chef_bio.background: The shop is the realization of a 13-year dream for owner-chef Takuya Kozasa, who trained for 13 years at the influential Kyoto Jiro-style house 'ラーメン荘 地球規模で考えろ／そら' (Ramen Sho 'Chikyu-kibo de Kangaero' / Sora) before striking out on his own. It opened on October 6, 2025, with 12 counter seats.
chef_bio.philosophy: Despite the big, brawny Jiro format, the cooking aims for balance — the soy tare is kept deliberately restrained in saltiness to let the broth's natural pork sweetness come through, tuned toward Kyoto palates, with garlic and a touch of chili (一味) for punch. The chef keeps refining the recipe by tracking room temperature and humidity day to day.
chef_bio.specialty: Jiro-style (二郎系) ramen built on house-made extra-thick, hand-massaged noodles (極太手揉み麺) cut on the shop's own noodle machine, in a sweet-edged pork-bone broth crowned with mounded vegetables, back fat (アブラ), garlic, and thick chashu. The standard bowl is 300g of noodles with two slices of pork; a flagship 'また此処ラーメン' with special toppings tops the menu. A brothless 'sojiru-nashi/tsukemen' version is also offered.

anecdotes.text: The name 'また此処で' (mata koko de — 'see you here again') doubles as the staff's parting line to guests: 'また此処でお待ちしています' ('we'll be waiting for you here again').

On opening, the shop announced the chef's roots plainly on social media: '元ソラの人です！地球規模で13年間修行してました！' ('I'm a former Sora guy — I trained for 13 years at Chikyu-kibo'), framing the launch as '13年間追い続けた夢が遂に動き出します' ('the dream I chased for 13 years finally takes off').

A call board (コール表) is posted at the counter so even newcomers to Jiro-style can pick their toppings — extra vegetables (野菜マシ), extra seasoning (カラメ), extra garlic — without having to call them out by heart.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi（eptC6）と osumituki（223370）が店主は地球規模／そら出身で13年修行・2025年10月6日開店・下京区西七条（赤もん跡地）・カウンター12席・極太手揉み麺の二郎系・コール表を確認。検索で店主名 小笹琢也 と300g/豚2枚の基本構成を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Core product is house-made extra-thick wheat noodles boiled in shared pots; gluten is unavoidable and there is no indication of any gluten-free handling.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tare is a soy-sauce-based (kaeshi) seasoning — standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat — kept light to let the pork-bone broth's sweetness show.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broth is pork-bone (tonkotsu) with back fat and pork toppings; vegetables are cooked into and mounded over the same animal-based bowl, so no component is free of animal contact.

cultural_comfort.note: A casual, counter-only neighborhood Jiro-style shop with a ticket machine and a posted call board, so a first-timer can point and order without much Japanese, though staff interaction is in Japanese and you'll be asked the standard "garlic?" question at the counter.

kyr_abura_soba_yumin.gf_detail: Not gluten-free / not celiac-safe. All bowls use wheat noodles (the regular and spicy abura soba use house-made wheat noodles; the back-fat vegetable bowl uses a thick Jiro-style wheat noodle), and the oil/tare sauce is a typical abura-soba sauce that contains wheat-based soy sauce. There is no gluten-free menu, no separate preparation, and no indication of allergy handling. A celiac diner should avoid this shop.
kyr_abura_soba_yumin.vegan_detail: No vegan option. This is an abura soba (brothless oil noodle) shop whose bowls center on a wheat-based oil/tare sauce, pork fat (背脂), char siu / fatty pork toppings, eggs, and mayo-based extras. The "背脂野菜油そば" (back-fat vegetable) bowl is built on pork fat in a Jiro style. No plant-based bowl is offered; a vegan diner could not be safely accommodated here.
kyr_abura_soba_yumin.hours_raw: 11:00–15:00 / 17:30–22:30 (Friday dinner until 22:00). Sources vary slightly on lunch close (one lists 11:00–14:30). Irregular closures announced on Instagram; some sources note Monday evening closed.
kyr_abura_soba_yumin.notes: [Mom & Pop] Yumin is the abura-soba spin-off of Bishiya (美しが), a ramen shop in Ichijoji known for drawing lines. The team opened this second, oil-noodle-focused shop in the Hyakumanben student quarter just north of the Hyakumanben crossing near Kyoto University, taking over a space that had

chef_bio.background: Yumin is the abura-soba spin-off of Bishiya (びし屋), a ramen shop in Ichijoji known for drawing lines. The team opened this second, oil-noodle-focused shop in the Hyakumanben student quarter just north of the Hyakumanben crossing near Kyoto University, taking over a space that had been a curry restaurant. Staff from the Ichijoji parent moved over to run it. It opened on October 10, 2025, and was generating buzz before it even opened.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make oil soba approachable: lighter on the palate than its rich look suggests, with a good balance of acidity and aromatics, and table signage that walks first-timers through how to eat it. Diners mix everything themselves, dial in garlic to taste, and use the counter condiments (vinegar, chili oil, pepper, diced onion) to shift the flavor partway through the bowl.
chef_bio.specialty: Abura soba — brothless wheat noodles tossed with an oil-and-tare sauce. Three bowls anchor the menu: the standard abura soba and a spicy version (辛味あぶらそば), both on house-made noodles, plus a 背脂ヤサイあぶらそば (back-fat vegetable) bowl built in a Jiro style on thick, chewy noodles with pork fat and a mound of vegetables. The base bowl is about 750 yen, with cheap noodle upsizes up to 540g.

anecdotes.text: The shop took over a former curry restaurant in Hyakumanben and was already a talking point among Kyoto ramen fans before opening, on the strength of the Bishiya name.
One writer summed up the bowl as 'lighter than it looks, with a good balance of acidity and seasonings,' and noted the table signage guiding newcomers through mixing and topping their noodles.
The back-fat vegetable bowl deliberately breaks from the plain look of typical oil soba, piling on Jiro-style pork fat and vegetables on a thick crinkly noodle.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi（taoZO）が一乗寺の行列店『びし屋』の2号店・百万遍（京大近く）のカレー店跡地・2025年10月10日開店・開店前から話題・3種（あぶらそば/辛味/背脂ヤサイ）・自家製麺・基本750円・食べ方POP・卓上調味料を確認。osumituki（223472）が背脂ヤサイの二郎系仕立てを確認。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The bowls are abura soba dressed in an oil-and-tare sauce of the standard type, which is based on wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is offered.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bowls are built on pork fat (背脂), fatty pork, eggs and mayo-based toppings shared across the kitchen; there is no plant-based bowl and no separation from animal ingredients.

cultural_comfort.note: A casual student-district ticket-machine shop where ordering and eating are wordless and self-directed, so basic Japanese (or just pointing at the machine) is plenty, but there is no English support or allergy accommodation.

kyr_taiwan_mazesoba_senmonte.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The core dish is Taiwanese mazesoba built on wheat noodles (the shop even lets you choose between two wheat-flour noodle types), tossed with a soy-sauce-based Taiwanese mince — both standard wheat-containing components. No gluten-free noodle, tare, or accommodation is mentioned anywhere. Celiac diners should treat this as unsafe.
kyr_taiwan_mazesoba_senmonte.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The menu centers on pork — signature 東坡肉 (skin-on braised pork belly / dongpo pork), spicy Taiwanese pork mince, chashu rice bowls, and a chicken-paitan ramen. Eggs (味玉) feature prominently. No plant-based bowl is advertised.
kyr_taiwan_mazesoba_senmonte.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–14:00, 18:00–21:00; Sat/Sun/holidays 11:00–21:00. Closed: irregular days off.
kyr_taiwan_mazesoba_senmonte.notes: [Mom & Pop] A specialty mazesoba shop that opened on November 20, 2024, on Senbon-dori. The signature dongpo-pork dish is prepared under a Chinese chef who keeps to an authentic recipe while tuning it to Japanese palates.

chef_bio.origin: Kyoto, Kamigyo-ku (Senbon-Demizu, northwest of Nijo Castle)
chef_bio.background: A specialty mazesoba shop that opened on November 20, 2024, on Senbon-dori. The signature dongpo-pork dish is prepared under a Chinese chef who keeps to an authentic recipe while tuning it to Japanese palates.
chef_bio.philosophy: Quality ingredients plus customization: the owner frames the two noodle choices as 'selecting the two ultimate options so you can enjoy Taiwanese mazesoba's deliciousness to the very end,' and sets out 10-plus condiments (garlic vinegar, kombu/anchovy vinegar and more) to encourage mid-meal 味変 (flavor-shifting).
chef_bio.specialty: 東坡肉台湾まぜそば — Taiwanese mazesoba crowned with dongpo pork (皮付きの豚の角煮, glossy skin-on braised pork belly slow-cooked with star anise). The house bills itself as Japan's first mazesoba shop that lets you pick your noodle, choosing between a medium-thick full-wheat noodle and a wavy 'wing' noodle so you can enjoy the bowl your way to the last bite.

anecdotes.text: The shop sources top-grade Kujo negi normally reserved for high-end kaiseki restaurants, and 'triple-folate' eggs from the Tanba/Mizuho area.
Beyond mazesoba the counter also serves a chicken-paitan ramen (泡鶏白湯拉麺) and chashu rice, with Taiwanese beer on offer to pair with the bowls.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The kitchen is built around wheat noodles and a soy-sauce-based Taiwanese mince; no gluten-free handling or separate prep is described, so heavy gluten cross-contact should be assumed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Taiwanese mazesoba tare is conventionally a wheat-based soy-sauce mince; no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Menu is pork- and egg-forward (dongpo pork, pork mince, chashu, 味玉); no vegan bowl, and shared equipment with meat dishes should be assumed.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny 6-seat neighborhood noodle counter with no indication of English service, so a few words of Japanese and pointing at the menu will make ordering smooth.

kyr_chikara_mochi_shokudo_ka.gf_detail: This is a traditional Showa-era noodle diner. The signature 中華そば uses fine wheat ramen noodles in a dashi-style broth, and the menu is built around wheat-based noodles (udon, soba, chūka soba), rice bowls and inari sushi. There is no indication of gluten-free preparation, dedicated equipment, or allergen handling. Broth and tare almost certainly involve wheat-containing soy sauce. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_chikara_mochi_shokudo_ka.vegan_detail: A meat-and-fish family diner: the 中華そば comes with thick char siu pork, two kinds of fish-cake kamaboko, and a dashi-based broth. Rice bowls and set meals are similarly animal-based. No vegan options are advertised and the kitchen is not set up for plant-based requests.
kyr_chikara_mochi_shokudo_ka.notes: [Mom & Pop] Part of the historic Rikimochi (力餅) lineage that began in 1889 in Toyooka as a confectionery and spread across Kansai as a franchise of homey eateries; fewer than a handful of these old shops survive today. This Kakichu branch was opened independently in 1966 (Showa 41) by the fo

chef_bio.chef_name: Seiji Kakichu (founder of this branch; run today by the proprietor couple)
chef_bio.background: Part of the historic Rikimochi (力餅) lineage that began in 1889 in Toyooka as a confectionery and spread across Kansai as a franchise of homey eateries; fewer than about ten of these old shops survive today. This Kakichu branch was opened in 1966 (Showa 41) by Seiji — the father of today's proprietor — under the Rikimochi name, and remains a fixture of the Fukakusa shopping street.
chef_bio.philosophy: あっさりと飽きのこない家庭的な味 — a light, never-tiring homestyle flavor served in an unpretentious old-fashioned shokudo where everything stays under 1,000 yen and a solo diner is always welcome.
chef_bio.specialty: 中華そば (chūka soba) at around 680 yen: a deliberately light, pale broth closer to a gentle udon dashi than a heavy ramen soup, with fine straight noodles, thick-cut char siu, two kinds of kamaboko fish cake, generous Kyoto negi and menma. Their oversized inari sushi (about 150 yen), packed with black sesame, carrot and burdock, is a beloved side.

anecdotes.text: The shop keeps a classic Showa-era atmosphere down to the television in the corner, and the owner couple know their regulars personally, trading easy small talk as customers come and go.
The 中華そば broth is so pale and gentle that it reads more like a soothing udon dashi than a typical ramen soup, the kind of bowl described as quietly soaking into your body.
Opened in 1966 by Seiji under the historic Rikimochi name, it is one of the dwindling number of these old Kansai diners still in operation.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi（GZjPd）が力餅の系譜（1889年豊岡の菓子屋に始まりフランチャイズで関西へ、現在10店未満）・この深草店は1966年（昭和41年）にせいじさんが開業・約680円の淡麗な中華そば（うどん出汁のよう、細ストレート麺、厚切りチャーシュー、2種のかまぼこ、京ねぎ、メンマ）・約150円の大きないなり（黒ごま・人参・ごぼう）・テレビのある昭和の雰囲気と常連客を確認。

vegan_cross_contact.text: Signature bowl uses char siu pork, fish-cake kamaboko and a dashi-based broth; no plant-based preparation indicated.

kyr_chuka_soba_roku.gf_detail: This is a refined chuka-soba (Chinese-style ramen) specialist. The dish is built on custom-made wheat noodles, almost certainly served with a wheat-based shoyu/Chinese-style tare, and a meat broth drawn from five bone stocks (duck, local chicken, venison, beef, pork). Wonton toppings are wheat-wrapped. No gluten-free menu, dedicated preparation, or wheat-free option is advertised on any source reviewed. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_chuka_soba_roku.vegan_detail: The entire concept is centered on an animal broth extracted from five types of bone (duck, free-range chicken, venison, beef, pork), and the signature wontons contain pork. There is no vegetarian or vegan ramen on the menu and no plant-based broth option. Not suitable for vegan or vegetarian diners.
kyr_chuka_soba_roku.hours_raw: Lunch 11:00-15:00 (L.O. 14:30) / Dinner 18:00-21:00 (L.O. 20:30). Closes early when the broth runs out.
kyr_chuka_soba_roku.notes: Roku is produced by chef Yuji Iwasaki, who earned two Michelin stars at his high-end Chinese restaurant VELROSIER. chef_bio.background: Roku is produced by chef Yuji Iwasaki, who earned two Michelin stars at his high-end Chinese restaurant VELROSIER. The shop began as 鴨出汁中華そば ROKU (kamo-dashi / duck-broth chuka-soba) and was renewed and renamed to 中華そば 六 when it reopened on the second floor of GOOD NATURE STATION on May 13, 2023, narrowing its focus to a single, refined Chinese-style noodle soup.
chef_bio.philosophy: Applying the techniques of fine Chinese cuisine to ramen to create what the shop calls a 唯一無二 (one-of-a-kind) soup — an elevated, restaurant-grade take on the everyday chuka-soba.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature 中華そば (Chuka Soba, around ¥1,100): a clear yet deeply layered broth that draws umami from five kinds of bone stock — duck, free-range chicken, venison, beef and pork — and builds further depth with porcini, longan fruit, tomato and dried shiitake. Straight noodles are custom-made to match the clear soup, and hand-made wontons (pork, onion, arrowhead and celery) are added partway through the bowl as a second act.

anecdotes.text: A two-Michelin-star Chinese chef (VELROSIER) channeling his craft into a tiny counter ramen shop, the bowl is engineered around Chinese stock technique rather than typical ramen broths — five animal bones layered with porcini, longan, tomato and shiitake.
The shop has been recognized in Michelin's Bib Gourmand listing for its chuka-soba.
Originally 鴨出汁中華そば ROKU, the restaurant relaunched as 中華そば 六 inside GOOD NATURE STATION on May 13, 2023, refocusing entirely on its Chinese-style noodle soup.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: goodnaturestation・kyotokurasu・lmaga・kyotopi より、ミシュラン二つ星『VELROSIER』オーナーシェフ岩崎祐司氏プロデュース、鴨・地鶏・鹿・牛・豚の5種のガラ＋ポルチーニ/龍眼肉/トマト/干し椎茸、追いワンタン（豚・玉ねぎ・クワイ・セロリ）、GOOD NATURE STATION 2Fで2023年5月13日リニューアル、ビブグルマン掲載を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The dish is wheat ramen noodles in a meat broth, with wheat-wrapped wontons, prepared in a small 12-seat shared kitchen; no gluten-free handling is advertised. Treat as not celiac-safe.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: As a Chinese-style chuka-soba, the tare is almost certainly soy/shoyu-based, which standardly contains wheat. No wheat-free seasoning is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The broth itself is animal-based (five bone stocks: duck, chicken, venison, beef, pork) and wontons contain pork, so there is no vegan-compatible base; cross-contact is moot because no plant-based option exists.

cultural_comfort.note: A small 12-seat counter ramen shop inside a modern, visitor-friendly retail complex (GOOD NATURE STATION) by Kyoto Kawaramachi Station, so it is approachable with basic greetings even if deep English support is not guaranteed.

kyr_kyo_kiyomizu_abura_soba_.gf_detail: Abura soba is a brothless wheat-noodle dish built on a soy-based (wheat) tare with sesame oil, topped with chashu pork — wheat is present in both the thick flat noodles and the tare. No gluten-free noodle or tamari option is advertised, and there is no indication of allergen accommodation. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_kyo_kiyomizu_abura_soba_.vegan_detail: The signature bowls are built on animal ingredients: diced chashu pork, soy-based tare, and toppings such as naruto (fish cake) and menma. No vegan or vegetarian version is mentioned. The side of 卵かけご飯 (egg-on-rice) is also non-vegan. Not suitable for vegans.
kyr_kyo_kiyomizu_abura_soba_.notes: [Mom & Pop] Billed as Kansai's first abura-soba specialty shop, this small noodle counter sits in the thick of the Kiyomizu tourist district, on Matsubara-dori between Gojo and Shijo, near the approach to Kiyomizu-dera.

chef_bio.background: Billed as Kansai's first abura-soba specialty shop, this small noodle counter sits in the thick of the Kiyomizu tourist district, on Matsubara-dori between Gojo and Shijo, near the approach to Kiyomizu-dera.
chef_bio.specialty: Abura soba — 'ramen without the soup.' Thick, flat kishimen-like noodles are tossed with a soy-based tare and fragrant sesame oil pooled at the bottom of the bowl, dressed with thick menma, diced chashu, green onion and naruto. The house signature is the 新元祖油そば (around 800 yen), and the lineup runs across soy, spicy-miso, and shrimp-salt versions, with a side of egg-on-rice (卵かけご飯) a popular add-on.

anecdotes.text: The shop hands you a little dish of minced raw onion to scatter on top — the way to eat it is to lift the tare up from the bottom of the bowl and mix everything thoroughly so noodles, toppings and sauce come together before you dig in; the onion adds sharpness and crunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi と食べログより、関西初の油そば専門店、松原通（五条〜四条）の清水観光地、きしめん風の平打ち麺、太メンマ・角切りチャーシュー・ねぎ・なると、新元祖油そば800円、辛味噌・海老塩などのバリエーション、卵かけご飯300円、刻み玉ねぎを添えて底からよく混ぜる食べ方を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat-based abura soba noodles and a soy (wheat) tare are the core of every bowl; no gluten-free preparation is offered or mentioned.
gf_cross_contamination.source_wording: 「きしめんのような平打ちの麺」／「もちもちの平うちの麺」 (kishimen is wheat) and 「こだわりの油そばは３種類、醤油風味、辛味噌、海老香る天然塩味です。」 — plus 「鶏天ぷらのついたセットメニューや串カツや水餃子などの単品メニューもあります。」

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The dish is built on a soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in standard Japanese practice contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bowls include diced chashu pork plus naruto fish cake and menma; no vegan/vegetarian version is described.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, casual tourist-area noodle counter where pointing at the picture menu and a friendly greeting will carry you through; do not expect English allergen support.

kyr_komugi_no_kirameki_kamik.gf_detail: This is a wheat-noodle ramen and mazesoba shop with its own on-site noodle factory, so the noodles are wheat-based; the chicken-paitan ramen and Taiwan mazesoba are built on wheat noodles plus a shoyu/tare seasoning that typically contains wheat. There is no indication of gluten-free noodles, dedicated equipment, or any celiac accommodation. Not suitable for someone who needs to avoid gluten.
kyr_komugi_no_kirameki_kamik.vegan_detail: The core menu is animal-based: chicken-paitan (tori-paitan) broth simmered from chicken, and Taiwan-style mazesoba topped with minced pork, egg yolk, chives and garlic, plus a back-fat "小麦のチカラ" with pork chunks. No vegan or vegetarian ramen is offered, and broths/tare are meat-based. Not a vegan-friendly option.
kyr_komugi_no_kirameki_kamik.hours_raw: 11:00-23:00 (L.O. 22:30) / Closed: none (may close temporarily on occasion)
kyr_komugi_no_kirameki_kamik.notes: [Mom & Pop] Komugi no Kirameki (Komugi) is one of the shops of the Kyoto-born ramen chain 'Kirameki Group' (operator: Kirameki no Mirai Co., Ltd.), a spacious suburban-style location along National Route 9 in Kamikatsura Maeda-cho. It is part of a group that expanded from its flagship brand 'Kirameki no Tori' in Marutamachi to across Kyoto City, Fukuchiyama, Ayabe, and further to Osaka (Suita, Takatsuki). A notable feature is the attached in-house noodle factory, visible through glass, where they make their own noodles.

roles: キラメキグループ店舗
chef_bio.background: コムギノキラメキ〈小麦〉は、京都発のラーメンチェーン「キラメキグループ」（運営：キラメキノ未来株式会社）の店舗のひとつで、上桂前田町の国道9号沿いに構える広々とした郊外型の一軒。本店ブランドである丸太町の「キラメキノトリ」から京都市内・福知山・綾部、さらに大阪（吹田・高槻）へと勢力を広げてきたグループの一翼で、店内にはガラス越しに見える自家製の製麺所を併設し、麺を自前で打っているのが大きな特徴。
chef_bio.philosophy: 自家製麺と濃厚な一杯で“小麦（コムギ）”そのものの力を主役にする、というコンセプトを店名に込め、子ども向けラーメンの用意やポイント制度など、地元のファミリーや一人客が気軽に通える普段使いの一杯を目指している。
chef_bio.specialty: 看板は二本立て。長時間炊き出した鶏のうまみが凝縮した白濁スープの『鶏白湯ラーメン』（醤油・塩あり）と、豚ミンチ・卵黄・ニラ・にんにくをのせたガツンと濃い『台湾まぜそば』。さらに背脂系で麺量を最大500gまで増やせる『小麦のチカラ』など、自家製の太麺を主役にした食べごたえ重視の品が揃う。

anecdotes.text: ガラス張りの製麺所を併設し、自家製の麺をその場で作っている様子が客席から見える。
鶏白湯スープは白濁してコクが強く、飲んだ後に舌へ粉末状のうまみがザラッと残るほど鶏が凝縮していると評される。
キラメキグループ5店舗目として国道9号沿いの上桂に出店し、使い勝手のよい郊外型の店として紹介されている。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: genjitsutouhi・kyotopi・公式より、キラメキグループ（キラメキノ未来株式会社）の5店舗目、上桂・国道9号沿いの郊外型店、ガラス張りの自家製製麺所（グループの製麺工房を兼ねる）、鶏白湯（醤油・塩）と台湾まぜそば、麺量最大500gの『小麦のチカラ』を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Self-described as a wheat-noodle shop ('コムギ／小麦') with an on-site noodle factory, so wheat is central and pervasive throughout the kitchen; no gluten-free option exists.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The chicken-paitan ramen is offered in a soy-sauce (醤油) variety; standard ramen shoyu tare is typically wheat-based, and no wheat-free seasoning is indicated.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All signature bowls are animal-based — chicken broth, minced pork, egg yolk; no vegan items are prepared, so there is no separated vegan line.

cultural_comfort.note: A bustling, family-friendly suburban ramen shop with a ticket-vending machine ordering system and no English menu, so a guide or translation help is useful for navigating toppings and noodle-portion choices.

kyr_chuka_rokuroku.gf_detail: Not gluten-free safe. The signature chuka-soba uses standard wheat ramen noodles in a soy-sauce (醤油) broth, and the wider menu (gyoza, fried chicken/karaage, shumai, stir-fries) leans heavily on wheat flour and wheat-based soy sauce. No gluten-free menu, no celiac accommodation, and no allergen handling is advertised.
kyr_chuka_rokuroku.vegan_detail: Not a vegan or vegetarian specialist. This is a meat-and-seafood town-Chinese kitchen — char siu, fried chicken, shrimp dumplings, crab omelette, pork trotters — and the ramen broth is animal-based. A few vegetable dishes exist (e.g. a zha cai/celery/dried-tofu salad, mapo-style and stir-fried items) but they typically use meat-based seasoning, soy sauce and shared woks, so a vegan would have to ask directly and expect very limited options.
kyr_chuka_rokuroku.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–13:45 (last order) / Dinner 17:30–21:00 (last order). Closed Mon. Hours are not clearly stated on Tabelog and some sources note irregular days off, so confirming via Facebook etc. before visiting is recommended.
kyr_chuka_rokuroku.notes: [Mom & Pop] 中華 六六 sits in a renovated Kyoto machiya just west of the Horikawa-Kitaoji crossing, in the Murasakino district a short walk from Daitoku-ji temple. The building once housed a Japanese restaurant; its high ceilings and shoes-off, eel's-nest layout — a few tables by the entrance an

chef_bio.background: 中華 六六 sits in a renovated Kyoto machiya just west of the Horikawa-Kitaoji crossing, in the Murasakino district a short walk from Daitoku-ji temple. Its high ceilings and shoes-off, eel's-nest layout — a few tables by the entrance and a long counter deep in the back — make a warm, retro setting for Chinese home-style cooking that locals treat as a townhouse take on neighborhood Chinese.
chef_bio.philosophy: A neighborhood kitchen that prizes authentic ingredients — its dried tofu is specially sourced from mainland China — and leans on volume and comfort over flash, the sort of filling, hospitable lunch that keeps regulars coming back.
chef_bio.specialty: The kitchen is known for hearty, generous lunch sets around 1,000 yen — a fried-chicken (yurin-chi) set, mapo and weekly-rotating set menus — alongside a soy-sauce chuka-soba. That bowl leads with a clean shoyu base carrying a gentle tang and the sweetness of scallion and onion, medium straight noodles, a thick slab of char siu, and menma that one local guide called the best they had ever eaten.

anecdotes.text: The traditional machiya architecture is as much the experience as the food — you take your shoes off at the entrance — the kind of townhouse Chinese ('町家中華') that sets it apart from a plain 町中華.
One diner stumbled on the shop walking back from Daitoku-ji, drawn in purely by the machiya frontage, and singled out the bamboo-shoot menma as the finest they had tasted.
A Kyoto food guide praised the volume-packed sub-1,000-yen lunches — 'お腹パンパン、ボリューム満点のランチ' — in a clean, nostalgic space favored by locals.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyoto-gourmet・kyotopi・digistyle より、紫野西御所田町（堀川北大路の西）の京町家を改装したレトロな中華店、靴を脱ぐ造り、1,000円前後・満腹のランチ、醤油中華そばの厚切りチャーシューと絶品メンマ、干し豆腐は本場中国から取り寄せ、を確認。前身が日本料理店だったとの記述は出典で確認できず削除。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled and animal/soy-based broth, gyoza and karaage are prepared in the same small kitchen, so heavy wheat cross-contact is unavoidable for a celiac.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The chuka-soba broth is built on a soy-sauce (醤油) base, which in a town-Chinese kitchen is standard wheat-containing soy sauce.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Menu is meat- and seafood-centered (char siu, fried chicken, shrimp dumplings, crab omelette, pork trotters) with shared woks; vegetable dishes likely use animal-based seasonings.

cultural_comfort.note: A neighborhood machiya Chinese spot where you remove your shoes at the door and order from a Japanese-only menu, so basic Japanese or a translation app and a relaxed attitude help a lot.

kyr_kirameki_no_tori.gf_detail: Not gluten-free safe. The ramen is built on in-house wheat noodles (made from 100% Hokkaido wheat at the group's own noodle workshop), and the menu also features Taiwan mazesoba (wheat) and karaage (wheat-dredged fried chicken). The chicken-paitan broth comes in shio/shoyu/miso tares; the shoyu and miso versions involve wheat-based soy sauce/miso. There is no published gluten-free preparation, dedicated equipment, or allergen-handling information. A celiac diner should not eat here.
kyr_kirameki_no_tori.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The entire concept is chicken: the broth is a chicken-bone paitan simmered with chicken thigh meat and skin, toppings include chicken-thigh chashu, and the shop is paired with karaage. No vegetable or plant-based broth or noodle option is published.
kyr_kirameki_no_tori.hours_raw: 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:30) / 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:30). Open daily, with occasional temporary closures.
kyr_kirameki_no_tori.notes: This is the original flagship (一号店) of Kirameki no Tori, opened in 2013 near the Kawaramachi-Marutamachi crossing in Kyoto's Kamigyo ward. From this single counter the brand grew into a chicken-focused group (operated by Kirameki no Mirai Co.) with around two dozen shops across K

chef_bio.background: This is the original flagship (一号店) of Kirameki no Tori, opened in 2013 just north of the Kawaramachi-Marutamachi crossing (Demizu-cho, Kamigyo ward) in Kyoto. From this single counter the brand grew into a chicken-focused group (operated by Kirameki no Mirai Co.) with around 30 shops across Kyoto, Osaka, Shiga and Nara, plus a noodle workshop in Nishikyo ward — but the Demizu-cho shop remains where it all started.
chef_bio.philosophy: Everything revolves around the chicken: the broth is built from chicken bones simmered with thigh meat and skin for a rich, sweet umami that is full-bodied without being heavy, and the noodles are made in-house from 100% Hokkaido wheat for a fragrant, crisp bite. The group's stated aim is to keep taste and service at a high level even as it expands.
chef_bio.specialty: Tori-paitan ramen — a creamy chicken white-broth bowl offered in shio, shoyu and miso. The signature shio version is finished with chicken-thigh chashu, white leek, mizuna, thread chili, menma and a slice of lemon for brightness. Taiwan mazesoba and karaage round out the menu.

anecdotes.text: The broth is made by carefully simmering chicken bones together with chicken thigh meat and skin, giving a soup with clear chicken richness and sweetness that avoids feeling overly heavy.
The noodles are produced at the group's own noodle workshop in Nishikyo ward using 100% Hokkaido wheat, prized for their aroma and crisp texture.
Opened in 2013 as the very first shop, it became the seed of a chicken-ramen group that now spans Kyoto, Osaka, Shiga and Nara.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi と公式（キラメキノ未来）より、2013年開業の出水町一号店（河原町丸太町すぐ）、西京区の自社製麺工房・北海道産小麦100%、塩ラーメンの具（鶏もも肉チャーシュー・白髪ねぎ・水菜・糸唐辛子・レモン・メンマ）、京都・大阪・滋賀・奈良に展開する鶏白湯グループ（公式店舗一覧では約33店）を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The kitchen handles wheat ramen noodles, Taiwan mazesoba (wheat noodles) and wheat-dredged karaage, so heavy gluten cross-contact is unavoidable in this environment.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The chicken-paitan bowls are offered in shoyu and miso versions, whose tare uses standard wheat-containing soy sauce/miso; even the shio version is a wheat-noodle dish.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The broth is a chicken-bone paitan simmered with chicken meat and skin and topped with chicken chashu; there is no plant-based broth or noodle option, so no vegan service is possible.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, busy local ramen counter with ticket-machine ordering and self-service water; a little Japanese or pointing helps, and no special accommodations should be expected.

kyr_otabi_hanten.gf_detail: No gluten-free provision. This is an old-school neighborhood Chinese diner whose core dishes — 中華そば (wheat ramen noodles), fried rice, gyoza, ankake/oyster-sauce stir-fries over rice (the signature 御旅丼) — all rely on wheat noodles, wheat-flour dumpling skins and soy-based (wheat-containing) seasonings, typically cooked on shared surfaces and woks. No dedicated gluten-free menu, prep, or fryer was found. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_otabi_hanten.vegan_detail: Not a vegan-friendly venue. The kitchen centers on pork, egg and seafood (the signature 御旅丼 is stir-fried pork, cabbage, carrot, onion, wood-ear and egg over rice; menu spans yakiniku, fried shrimp and gyoza). Broths and tare are meat/seafood based. No vegan dishes were identified, and there is no indication the kitchen can prepare a meaningful plant-based meal. A vegan diner should ask, but should not expect a workable option here.
kyr_otabi_hanten.hours_raw: 11:00–14:30, 17:30–23:00 (closed Wed). Some sources give lunch starting at 11:30 and dinner ending at 22:00.
kyr_otabi_hanten.notes: [Mom & Pop] 御旅飯店 is a long-standing neighborhood Chinese diner (町中華) tucked into the old Kitaoji-Omiya quarter near Funaokayama and the Daitokuji temple precinct. Its name comes from the adjacent 御旅所 (otabi-sho) — the resting place for the portable shrine during Imamiya Shrine's festival eac

chef_bio.background: 御旅飯店 is a long-standing neighborhood Chinese diner (町中華) tucked into the old Kitaoji-Omiya quarter near Funaokayama and the Daitokuji temple precinct. Its name comes from the adjacent 御旅所 (otabi-sho) — the resting place for the portable shrine during Imamiya Shrine's festival each May. This pocket of the city flourished as a merchant district in the Edo period and quieted after the early Showa era as the Nishijin textile trade declined, leaving behind exactly the kind of unhurried local shop the restaurant still embodies.
chef_bio.philosophy: Hearty, affordable, community-first cooking — big portions, free rice refills, and a deep two-sided menu of Chinese standards (fried rice, gyoza, noodles, fried and grilled dishes) priced for everyday eating.
chef_bio.specialty: The house pride is the 御旅丼 (Otabi-don), a local bowl that is, in the words of one writer, 'barely known outside the neighborhood': stir-fried pork with cabbage, carrot, onion, wood-ear mushroom and egg, bound in a Chinese-style sauce over a generous mound of rice (said to hold roughly three servings). The shop also serves a proper 中華そば and offers ramen as an add-on to many dishes.

anecdotes.text: The shop sits right by the otabi-sho used during Imamiya Shrine's May festival, which is where its name '御旅' comes from.

It is a narrow, old-school place with counter seats and small tatami sections, stocked with comics, magazines and a TV, full of neighborhood workers and university students; staff move briskly through the lunch rush.
Rice refills are free, and the kitchen still runs deliveries the old way using traditional okamochi carrying boxes.
Known locally for big, well-balanced portions, including the signature 御旅丼.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi と gcjapan より、今宮神社の御旅所が店名の由来、江戸期に商家町として栄え昭和期に西陣衰退で静かになった一帯の町中華、御旅丼（豚肉・野菜・卵の中華餡でご飯約3杯分・かなりローカル）、ご飯おかわり無料、岡持ちでの出前、カウンター＋小上がりで漫画・雑誌・TVありの雰囲気を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat ramen noodles, wheat-flour gyoza skins and soy-based seasonings dominate the menu, cooked on shared woks and surfaces in a small kitchen — high cross-contact risk for gluten throughout.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Dishes are seasoned with Chinese-style soy/oyster sauces (the 御旅丼 sauce is described as a Chinese sauce/oyster-sauce base); standard Japanese and Chinese soy sauces contain wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Cooking centers on pork, egg and seafood across stir-fries, fried rice and gyoza; broths and sauces are meat/seafood based, so any vegetable dish would share equipment and seasonings with animal ingredients.

cultural_comfort.note: A no-frills local Chinese diner where Japanese-language ordering and casual local manners are the norm; a friendly spot but expect little to no English support.

kyr_iicho_ramen.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. The bowl is built on wheat ramen noodles (from Rairaiken/Kairaikian seimen) and a wheat-based soy sauce tare (Sawai twice-fermented "double-koji" shoyu), with no gluten-free menu or allergen accommodation noted anywhere. Treat as off-limits for strict gluten avoidance.
kyr_iicho_ramen.vegan_detail: Not vegan or vegetarian friendly. The signature broth is a chicken-bone and pork-bone blend (roughly 7:3) with back fat and sliced chashu pork; the popular yakimeshi side uses egg and pork fat. No plant-based option is offered.
kyr_iicho_ramen.hours_raw: 11:00-15:30 (L.O. 15:00); closes early if sold out. Lunch-only operation since February 2025. Closed Wednesday and Thursday plus occasional irregular closures. (Prior to Feb 2025 also served dinner 17:30-21:00, L.O. 20:30.)
kyr_iicho_ramen.notes: [Mom & Pop] Iicho opened in 1998 in the Shimogamo neighborhood of Sakyo-ku, a short walk east of Kitaoji across the Kamogawa. The shop carries on the lineage of the so-called 'phantom Iwakura ramen' (幻の岩倉ラーメン), a Kyoto street-cart ramen whose flavor passed to Yamasan Ramen before that shop e

chef_bio.background: Iicho opened in 1998 in the Shimogamo neighborhood of Sakyo-ku, a short walk east of Kitaoji across the Kamogawa. The shop carries on the lineage of the so-called 'phantom Iwakura ramen' (幻の岩倉ラーメン), a Kyoto street-cart ramen whose flavor passed to Yamasan Ramen before that shop eventually moved away to Shiga; the founder learned the style from that tradition and brought it into the modern era.
chef_bio.philosophy: The proprietor sums up his approach as 'people are moved by heart,' treating each day's open as the start of a fresh battle and refining the bowl through constant, patient improvement.
chef_bio.specialty: An assari shoyu chuka-soba: a lightly cloudy broth of chicken bone (specifically the shin) and pork bone in roughly a 7:3 ratio, finished with back fat, thin chashu, and Kyoto negi. The tare is Sawai shoyu, a twice-fermented 'double-koji' soy sauce that gives the bowl its punchy backbone. Medium-thin straight noodles from Rairaiken keep an old-Showa chuka-soba character. The egg-and-pork-fat yakimeshi, with heavily caramelized edges, is a beloved companion.

anecdotes.text: The recipe descends from the legendary Iwakura cart ramen, later carried by Yamasan Ramen; Iicho opened in 1998 to keep that disappearing flavor alive.
The broth leans on aged chicken rather than young birds for deeper flavor, with small pork bones added gradually to build umami and exacting quality checks on the ingredients.
The kitchen has used the same Rairaiken (来々軒) noodles since opening, aiming to keep a strong nostalgic Showa-era chuka-soba feel while still tasting contemporary.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイトと osumituki より、1998年下鴨（左京区）開業、幻の岩倉ラーメン→山さんラーメン（後に滋賀へ移転）の系譜、『人は心で動く』の理念、鶏（すね）と豚骨7:3・老鶏使用・背脂・薄切りチャーシュー・京ねぎ、澤井醤油の二度仕込みダレ、来々軒の中細ストレート麺、玉子と豚脂の焦がし焼き飯を確認。麺屋名の別表記『Kairaikian』は出典になく削除。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The bowl is built on wheat ramen noodles and a wheat soy-sauce (Sawai shoyu) tare, so gluten is central to the dish; no gluten-free preparation is offered.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tare is Sawai shoyu, a twice-fermented double-koji soy sauce, which is wheat-based.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broth is chicken-bone and pork-bone based with back fat and chashu; the yakimeshi uses egg and pork fat. No vegan/vegetarian item exists, so all cooking surfaces and stock are animal-based.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, classic neighborhood ramen counter where a few words of Japanese and an easygoing attitude go a long way; no English service is advertised, so a friendly konnichiwa and pointing at the menu work best.

kyr_menya_homare.gf_detail: This is a standard wheat-noodle ramen and mazesoba shop. Noodles are wheat (from maker 麺屋棣鄂), the tare is a soy-sauce (typically wheat-containing) shoyu base, and the broth is a concentrated pork-bone-and-chicken stock. There is no indication of gluten-free noodles, dishes, or accommodation. Not celiac-safe.
kyr_menya_homare.vegan_detail: Every documented bowl is built on an animal base: a concentrated pork-bone (豚骨) and chicken (鶏ガラ) broth, with toppings such as chashu pork, ajitsuke (egg) tamago, and karaage. No vegetarian or vegan ramen option is mentioned anywhere in the sources.
kyr_menya_homare.hours_raw: Mon/Tue/Wed 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:30) / Fri/Sat 11:00–15:00 & 18:00–21:30 (last order 21:00) / closed Thu & Sun. Tabelog also lists Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat 11:00–14:00, 17:30–21:00 and Wed 11:00–14:00, 17:00–21:00; hours differ by source.
kyr_menya_homare.notes: [Mom & Pop] 麺屋 誉 (Menya Homare) opened on October 22, 2025 as the reborn version of a neighborhood favorite, フカクサ製麺食堂 (Fukakusa Seimen Shokudo). chef_bio.background: 麺屋 誉 (Menya Homare) opened on October 22, 2025 as the reborn version of a neighborhood favorite, フカクサ製麺食堂 (Fukakusa Seimen Shokudo). That predecessor began life humbly as a mazesoba specialist tucked into the corner of a parking lot, later moved into a proper storefront, and built a following on chicken-paitan (鶏白湯) ramen. When it closed at the end of September 2025, the shop reopened weeks later under the new Homare name with a completely retooled bowl.
chef_bio.philosophy: A carefully tended broth above all: 豚骨と鶏ガラを手間暇かけた濃厚スープは雑味が少なく、まろやかでとろみのある — a long-simmered pork-and-chicken stock prized for being rich yet clean, with little harshness and a smooth, slightly thick body. Bowls can be tuned to the guest, with noodle firmness, broth saltiness, and chicken-oil volume adjustable to taste.
chef_bio.specialty: 特製濃厚豚骨醤油ラーメン — a concentrated pork-bone-and-chicken soy-sauce ramen with a soy-forward, punchy, smooth and full-bodied broth. The default bowl arrives with two kinds of chashu (a thick, smoky pork and a black-pepper pastrami-style loin), a half-cooked ajitsuke egg, a blend of spinach/komatsuna greens, and sheets of nori, over straight medium-thick custom noodles from the long-established maker 麺屋棣鄂 (Teigaku).

anecdotes.text: The shop carries forward two things from its フカクサ製麺食堂 days: the popular まぜそば, and a per-piece karaage that guests order by the number (about ¥100 each).
A student discount lets those with a student ID upgrade to a large noodle portion for free — and it applies to the mazesoba too.
The new 濃厚豚骨醤油 bowl reads less like classic Iekei family-style ramen and more like a straight, intense pork-bone-soy ramen, with the soy notes leading.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: osumituki・kyotopi・noodlers より、2025年10月22日開業、前身フカクサ製麺食堂（2025年9月末閉店、鶏白湯で人気）のリニューアル、豚骨＋鶏ガラの濃厚豚骨醤油、低温調理の2種チャーシュー（燻香の豚と黒胡椒パストラミ）、ほうれん草・白ねぎ・海苔3枚、麺屋棣鄂（1931年創業）の中太ストレート麺、まぜそばと1個約100円の唐揚げを継続、学割で麺大盛り無料、伏見深草・藤森駅近くを確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat ramen noodles, a soy-sauce-based tare, and shared broth/cooking water make cross-contamination with gluten effectively unavoidable for a celiac diner.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature bowl is a 濃厚豚骨醤油 (pork-bone soy-sauce) ramen; the tare is soy-sauce based, which in standard ramen contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All broths and dishes are animal-based (pork bone and chicken stock with chashu, egg, and karaage); no vegan preparation or separation is described.

cultural_comfort.note: A small local counter ramen shop with cash-only payment and no reservations; some basic Japanese helps for ordering and customization, with little to no English support expected.

kyr_wamen_guriko_kyoto_honte.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. The custom noodles are made from domestic wheat flour, and the kitchen handles wheat throughout. While the bowls are salt-based (shio) rather than soy-sauce-based, there is no gluten-free menu, no dedicated preparation area, and the same broth/noodle line is used for all dishes. Cross-contact with wheat is unavoidable. The shop also offers a separate fresh-soy-sauce (生醤油) ramen, which would contain wheat. No GF accommodation is advertised.
kyr_wamen_guriko_kyoto_honte.vegan_detail: Not suitable for vegans or vegetarians. Both signature bowls are animal-based: the chicken-salt (鶏塩) broth is an eight-hour chicken consommé (with added shijimi clam at the Kyoto branch), and the sea-bream-salt (鯛塩) broth is built on wild domestic sea bream. The shio tare also layers in bonito (katsuo) dashi. Toppings include chashu pork and egg. No plant-based broth or vegan bowl is offered.
kyr_wamen_guriko_kyoto_honte.hours_raw: 11:00–22:00 daily (L.O. 21:30); through-service. May close earlier when the soup/ingredients sell out.

chef_bio.origin: Okayama (original shop); the chef trained in Tokyo
chef_bio.background: Chef Sho Isogai came up as an Italian cook before turning to ramen, apprenticing at celebrated Tokyo shops including Mensho. In 2017 he opened his own 麺処ぐり虎 (Mendokoro Guriko) in Okayama, which went on to earn a Michelin Bib Gourmand and repeat recognition across the Kyoto, Osaka and Okayama guides, plus top finishes at national ramen festivals and appearances at the Tokyo Ramen Show. 和麺ぐり虎 is his second brand, and this Kyoto branch on Rokkaku-dori opened on July 23, 2025 as his first foray into Kyoto.
chef_bio.philosophy: Isogai approaches ramen 'like a course,' marrying Italian and Japanese technique and deliberately restraining seasoning so the integrity of carefully chosen ingredients comes through. The 和麺 (wamen) concept centers on preserving and nurturing Japan's exceptional ingredients and food culture.
chef_bio.specialty: Two salt (shio) bowls define the shop. The 鶏塩 (chicken-salt) is a clear, eight-hour chicken consommé — deepened at the Kyoto branch with shijimi clam — finished with a house salt tare that blends salts from Japan, Italy, France and Mongolia and a layered dashi of kombu, shiitake and bonito. The 鯛塩 (sea-bream-salt) showcases wild domestic sea bream cooked low and slow for a clean, aromatic, umami-deep broth, with a tare built on Okinawan and Niigata sea salts. Custom thin straight noodles made from 100% domestic wheat are matched to the soups.

anecdotes.text: The chef's Italian-kitchen roots shape the salt tare, which draws on salts from Japan, Italy, France and Mongolia — an unusually cosmopolitan seasoning for a Japanese shio ramen.
The Kyoto branch's chicken-salt bowl adds shijimi clam to the eight-hour chicken consommé for extra depth while keeping the seasoning restrained.
Raw/boiled egg and nori are offered freely at the tables alongside any bowl.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: PR TIMES・gcjapan より、イタリアン出身で麺庄（Mensho）で修業した礒貝翔氏、2017年岡山で麺処ぐり虎を開業しビブグルマン・東京ラーメンショー出場、第二ブランド和麺ぐり虎の京都本店が2025年7月23日六角通に開業、鶏塩は8時間の鶏コンソメ＋しじみ・日本/イタリア/フランス/モンゴルの塩ダレ、鯛塩は国産天然真鯛・沖縄/新潟の塩、国産小麦100%の細麺を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Custom noodles are made from 100% domestic wheat flour and are handled throughout the kitchen; there is no gluten-free option or separate preparation, so wheat cross-contact is unavoidable.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature bowls are salt-based (shio) rather than soy-sauce-based; however, a separate fresh-soy-sauce (生醤油) ramen is also offered, which would contain wheat-based soy sauce.

source_independence.note: This source reprints shop marketing rather than reporting a visit (a curated hub or a press release). It corroborates that a claim was MADE, not that it was verified.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All broths are animal-based (chicken consommé with clam, or wild sea bream) and the tare includes bonito dashi; no plant-based broth is prepared, so there is no vegan-safe bowl.

positives.text: Bowls are shio (salt) tare rather than the usual wheat-shoyu tare, so the base seasoning is comparatively lower in soy/wheat than many ramen — though the wheat noodles still rule it out for celiacs.

cultural_comfort.note: A modern, welcoming counter-and-table ramen shop where ordering is done by QR code at the table, so a few words of Japanese and a friendly greeting go a long way, though the visual menu makes it manageable.

kyr_men_ya_tori_no_keiji_kyo.gf_detail: Standard ramen: wheat (medium-thick wavy) noodles plus shio/shoyu tare that typically contains wheat-based soy sauce. No gluten-free noodle or dedicated-handling options are advertised, and rice-bowl sides also involve sauces. Not safe for celiac diners; treat as not gluten-free.
kyr_men_ya_tori_no_keiji_kyo.vegan_detail: This is a chicken-paitan specialist; the entire concept is a broth simmered for 8+ hours from domestic chicken and water, with chicken chashu toppings. There are no plant-based broth or noodle options noted. Not suitable for vegans or vegetarians.
kyr_men_ya_tori_no_keiji_kyo.hours_raw: 10:30-00:30 daily (L.O. food 00:00); closes when soup runs out. Lunch sets 10:30-15:00, dinner sets 15:00-21:00.

chef_bio.background: An Osaka-born chicken-paitan specialist that built a reputation for long queues at its original shop and grew into a small group (with locations across the Osaka/Sakai area, Nara and Tokyo) before opening this, its first Kyoto outpost, on September 12, 2025, on a busy corner near Shijo-Kiyamachi just steps from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station.
chef_bio.philosophy: Let the chicken speak for itself: a broth built from only chicken and water, then aerated so the richness lands light and silky rather than heavy.
chef_bio.specialty: The house style is an 泡系 (foam-style) chicken paitan: fresh domestic chicken and water simmered for over eight hours into a thick, creamy stock that is whipped/aerated to order into a frothy, cappuccino-like soup, served over smooth medium-thick wavy noodles with low-temperature chicken chashu (both breast and thigh). It anchors a lineup of variations including tori-shio and tori-shoyu, Fromage (cheese), Truffle, Red (chili oil), Black (mayu/burnt garlic oil) and Green (matcha), plus chicken rice-bowl sides.

anecdotes.text: Described as a popular Osaka shop known for daily queues, making this Kyoto location its first foray into the city, opening September 12, 2025.
The broth is made from only fresh domestic chicken and water, simmered for over eight hours, then blended/aerated just before serving into an 'awa-awa' (foamy) finish.
The Kyoto store launched with upgraded versions of the signature chicken paitan and items available only at this location.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi・keiji-project より、大阪発の行列人気店、京都初出店は2025年9月12日（四条木屋町・京都河原町駅すぐ）、国産鶏と水のみを8時間以上炊きブレンダーで泡立てる泡系鶏白湯、中太ウェーブ麺・低温調理の鶏チャーシュー（むね/もも）、鶏塩・鶏醤油・Fromage・Truffle・Red・Black・Greenのバリエーションを確認。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Tori-shoyu (soy-sauce) bowls use a soy-based tare; Japanese shoyu is normally brewed with wheat. No gluten-free tare is advertised.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All broths are chicken-based (chicken + water simmered 8+ hours) and toppings include chicken chashu, so there is no vegan-safe preparation; cross-contact with animal stock is inherent to every bowl.

cultural_comfort.note: A modern, central ramen shop with QR-code mobile ordering, so a tourist can manage with minimal Japanese, but the interface and staff are primarily Japanese-oriented.

kyr_gyoza_dokoro_takatsuji_s.gf_detail: A gyoza specialist whose signature Sukemasa gyoza is wrapped in a springy special wheat skin; no gluten-free accommodation. The blended dipping sauces of Japanese dashi and miso as well as seasonings are highly likely to contain wheat-derived components, so it is not suitable for those requiring strict gluten-free such as celiac disease. No official information on gluten-free or wheat-allergy accommodation could be confirmed.
kyr_gyoza_dokoro_takatsuji_s.vegan_detail: The main product is meat gyoza using minced Kyo-mochibuta pork, and the Japanese dashi is bonito-based. Many Kyoto vegetables such as Kujo leek are used, but no gyoza or menu for vegans/vegetarians could be confirmed. There is no clear plant-based menu; whether accommodation is possible must be inquired about.
kyr_gyoza_dokoro_takatsuji_s.hours_raw: Weekdays 11:30-14:00 (L.O.) / 17:00-22:00 (L.O.); Sat, Sun & holidays 11:30-22:00 (L.O.); no regular closing day (open daily). Times shown are on a last-order basis.
kyr_gyoza_dokoro_takatsuji_s.notes: [Mom & Pop] A Kyoto-gyoza specialist proclaiming 'born and raised in Kyoto,' with its main shop along Takatsuji-dori close to Shijo Karasuma. Operated by MASTERMIND Inc., it insists on making gyoza from Kyoto-produced ingredients as a matter of local production for local consumption.

roles: テイクアウト・冷凍餃子販売
chef_bio.background: 「京都生まれ京都育ち」を掲げる京餃子の専門店で、四条烏丸にほど近い高辻通沿いに本店を構えます。運営はMASTERMIND社で、地産地消を信条に京都産の食材で餃子をつくることにこだわっています。
chef_bio.philosophy: 中華の調味料ではなく和のだしと味噌で仕上げる『和のぎょうざ』。にんにくの匂いを抑え、たれをほとんど付けずに素材の味で食べられるよう、女性や幅広い層が楽しめる上品な味わいを目指しています。
chef_bio.specialty: 看板の『亮昌ぎょうざ』。鰹だしをベースにした合わせ和だしで上品に仕立てた京もち豚のミンチに、香り豊かな九条ねぎを合わせ、隠し味に老舗『山利』の味噌をほんのり効かせ、もちもちの特製の皮で包んでいます。

anecdotes.text: 京都市長賞を受賞した伏見・中嶋農園のキャベツや京もち豚、京の伝統野菜である九条ねぎなど、できる限り京都の地のものを使用している。
黒く焙煎した七味と千鳥酢のたれが添えられ、にんにくの匂いを抑えて食べやすいと評される。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト・v-trip・食べログより、運営MASTERMIND社・エグゼクティブシェフ毛利亮氏、中華調味料を使わず鰹だしと山利の田舎味噌で仕立てる和のぎょうざ、にんにくの匂いを抑えた上品な味、京もち豚・九条ねぎ・伏見中嶋農園（京都市長賞）のキャベツなど地産地消、黒煎り七味と千鳥酢のたれを確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 餃子専門店であり、すべての主力商品が小麦の皮を使用するため、厨房は小麦が常用される環境です。グルテンフリー対応・分離調理に関する記載は確認できませんでした。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: 和だしと味噌をベースにしたたれや調味料を使用しており、醤油・味噌など小麦を含みうる発酵調味料が用いられている可能性があります。具体的な原材料の公開情報は確認できませんでした。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 京もち豚のミンチや鰹だしを中核に使用する肉餃子の専門店で、植物性メニューの分離・専用調理に関する情報は確認できませんでした。

positives.text: 英語メニューを用意しており、にんにく不使用の餃子のため、にんにくを避けたい人には案内しやすい。

cultural_comfort.note: 英語メニューを用意しており、四条烏丸の人気餃子専門店として観光客にも慣れているため、英語のみでも比較的安心して利用できます。

kyr_chuka_ryori_taiho.gf_detail: No gluten-free accommodation. This is a Chinese kitchen built around wheat: the ramen and tantanmen use wheat noodles, dumplings/dim sum are wheat-wrapped, and dishes are seasoned with wheat-based soy sauce and Chinese sauces. Broths and stir-fries are meat/seafood based and not designed for celiac safety. No dedicated fryer or allergen protocol is documented. Not suitable for strict gluten-free diners.
kyr_chuka_ryori_taiho.vegan_detail: Not a vegan-friendly venue. The menu centers on pork (the signature teri-don is glazed pork), wagyu mapo tofu, chicken, shrimp and other seafood, and meat/seafood-based broths and tare. Even ostensibly vegetable dishes are likely cooked with shared woks, meat fats and animal-based seasonings. No vegan options are documented.
kyr_chuka_ryori_taiho.hours_raw: 11:30-14:15 (lunch L.O. ~14:20), 17:30-21:00 (dinner L.O. ~20:30); closed Tuesdays plus irregular/biweekly Wednesdays. Sources vary slightly on the dinner close time (20:30-22:30 reported across listings); confirm by phone for late dinner.

chef_bio.background: Taiho opened in 1974 near Nijo Station and has been a fixture of Kyoto's machi-chuka (neighborhood Chinese) scene for about half a century. It began as a classic town-Chinese counter serving ramen, fried rice, gyoza and other everyday favorites; over the years the second-generation cook traveled to Sichuan in China and brought authentic Sichuan techniques back into the kitchen, gradually turning the shop into a place where old-school Kyoto machi-chuka and genuine Sichuan cooking sit side by side on the same menu.
chef_bio.philosophy: Bridging humble Kyoto town-Chinese comfort food with serious Sichuan cooking - keeping the beloved old standards like teri-don while layering in authentic regional Chinese flavors.
chef_bio.specialty: The house signature is the 'teri-don' (teridon) - a rice bowl crowned with sweet-savory teriyaki-glazed pork. It comes in several forms, most famously the 'teri-don kinshi' topped with shredded egg, plus an oversized 'jigoku-mori' (hell portion) for big appetites. Alongside it the menu spans ramen and chuka-soba, dan-dan noodles, hot-and-sour noodles, fried rice, tenshin-han and Chinese rice bowls, and Sichuan plates like mapo tofu made with Omi-area wagyu and sweet-and-sour pork.

anecdotes.text: Founded in 1974 and marking its 50th anniversary, Taiho has earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is known as a small shop with a near-constant queue at both lunch and dinner.

The second-generation cook visited Sichuan and introduced new dishes, transforming what was a standard machi-chuka into a place where town-Chinese and Sichuan cuisine are combined; the original teri-don remains the signature.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: v-trip・kyotopi・gcjapan より、1974年創業・二条駅近く・ミシュランビブグルマン・親子2代の行列町中華で、創業当初は町中華の定番中心だったが2代目が中国四川に足を運び四川料理を導入、名物てりどん／てりどんきんし／地獄盛り、近江牛の麻婆豆腐、担々麺・酸辣湯麺を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat-based noodles (ramen, chuka-soba, dan-dan, hot-and-sour noodles) and wheat-wrapped dumplings/dim sum are core to the menu, with heavy use of wheat soy sauce and Chinese sauces in a shared wok kitchen - high gluten exposure throughout.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Chinese-style cooking with soy and bean-paste seasonings; standard wheat-containing soy sauce should be assumed. No wheat-free tare or sauce is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Menu is built on pork, wagyu, chicken and seafood, with meat/seafood broths and shared woks; vegetable dishes are very likely cooked with animal fats and meat-based seasonings.

cultural_comfort.note: A busy local Chinese eatery with Japanese-language menus and no indication of English support, so a little Japanese or pointing at the menu helps; come ready to queue and order quickly at peak times.

kyr_kyoto_wamen_yukichi_honp.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. The bowls are built on wheat ramen noodles with a soy/dashi tare and chicken-scallop broth; no gluten-free menu or accommodation is advertised. Avoid if you require strict GF.
kyr_kyoto_wamen_yukichi_honp.vegan_detail: Not a vegan-friendly option. The entire concept centers on chicken-and-scallop dashi broth topped with A5 wagyu beef steak; there is no vegan ramen or plant-based offering.
